tldr: Users can now delete many folders in a single request. The items in those folders stay in the vault with no folder, on SQL Server and on the EF databases.
goal: Let a client clean up many folders at once, in place of 1 delete request per folder.

story.heading: 1 port, 2 adapters: IFolderRepository.DeleteManyAsync
story.body: The Vault port now deletes many folders. Dapper implements it on SQL Server and Entity Framework on PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite.

story.heading: DELETE /folders added
story.body: The endpoint takes a list of folder ids. Cloud requests take up to 500 ids. The VFO1Foundation feature flag gates it.

story.heading: DeleteManyFoldersCommand added to Vault
story.body: It keeps only the folders the user owns, deletes them and pushes a single vault sync to the user's clients.

story.heading: Both adapters clear the items, then delete the folders
story.body: Dapper calls Folder_DeleteByIds, which clears each item with JSON_MODIFY in a transaction. Entity Framework does the same in LINQ.

story.heading: The whole change
story.body: The change follows the ports and adapters rule: API, then Vault, then 2 adapters. Core references no infrastructure.

components.summary: New DELETE /folders endpoint and FolderBulkDeleteRequestModel, with a limit of 500 ids on cloud.
FolderRepository.DeleteManyAsync calls Folder_DeleteByIds in a transaction.
FolderRepository.DeleteManyAsync removes the folders and clears them from filed items; DeleteAsync uses it.
New Folder_DeleteByIds stored procedure and its migration script.

decisions.title: 1 port, 2 adapters
decisions.why: Core references no infrastructure. The port in Vault defines the behavior, and Dapper and EF give it to SQL Server and to PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite.
decisions.alternative: Call DeleteAsync once per folder from the command.

decisions.title: SQL Server does the work in a stored procedure
decisions.why: A single round trip updates the items and deletes the folders in a single transaction, as the other SQL Server repositories do.
decisions.alternative: Load the items in C# and update them, as EF does.

decisions.title: Ids the user does not own are ignored
decisions.why: The command filters the user's own folders. A request with other ids deletes nothing else and does not fail.
decisions.alternative: Refuse the whole request when an id is not the user's.

decisions.title: A single vault sync in place of 1 notification per folder
decisions.why: A delete also moves the items out of the folders. The clients need the whole vault again, not only the folder ids.
decisions.alternative: Push 1 folder delete notification per folder.

decisions.title: A limit of 500 ids, on cloud only
decisions.why: The cloud API caps the cost of a request. A self-hosted server has no limit.
decisions.alternative: The same limit for every server.
